name: Bicep and tricep implants

card.summary: Surgically placed silicone implants that add size and shape to the upper arms for people who want bigger-looking arms.
card.note: Surgical procedure with implant-related complications; discussed in bodybuilding forums with mixed reactions.

quick.overview:
Bicep and tricep implants are solid silicone shapes placed by a plastic surgeon to add volume to the upper arm. They are part of the same body-contouring family as calf, pectoral and deltoid implants.

The appeal is fuller, more defined arms for people who feel training has not given them the size they want. Forum discussions, including a T Nation feature on implants in bodybuilding, treat them as a surgical shortcut to the look of bigger muscle.
quick.how: A surgeon places the implant through an incision, usually near the muscle, after consultation and imaging. Forum users mention surgeons who advertise multiple implant types including bicep, tricep, deltoid, pec, calf and hip. Healing involves a recovery period before returning to training.
quick.risks: Surgery carries general risks such as infection, bleeding and scarring, and implants can shift or need removal. Bodybuilding commentators on T Nation describe some mixed or negative reactions to implants and synthol-type approaches.

lead: Bicep and tricep implants, also called arm implants, are silicone implants placed in the upper arm to add visible size.[1] The idea is to create the appearance of larger or more defined arms without the training time needed to add muscle.

Online, they come up in bodybuilding and T Nation threads, where users list bicep, tricep, deltoid, pec, calf and hip implants as options offered by body implant surgeons,[2] and one answer to a question about building bigger arms suggests bicep, tricep and deltoid implants.[3] T Nation has also run a feature on biceps and triceps implants, silicone abs and plastic lats and delts in bodybuilding.[1]
Reactions in these communities vary, with some commenters comparing implants and synthol unfavorably to natural training.[4][5] No clinical studies specific to arm implants have been identified.

chain: Silicone implant placed near arm muscle
angle.text: The implant adds contour to the arm without relying on muscle growth. People considering it are aiming for visibly bigger biceps or triceps.

paras: A T Nation feature titled 'Big Plastic Muscles' discusses biceps and triceps implants and other implants as part of a 'faux physique'.[1] In other threads, users mention implant surgeons' websites,[2] suggest implants for stubborn body parts,[3] or criticize implants and synthol as fake.[4][5]

lore.intro: Implants appear in bodybuilding forums as a surgical alternative for lagging muscle groups, with both interest and criticism.[1][4]

claims.claim: Implants can give bigger arms without more training
claims.believers: Posters list surgeons offering bicep and tricep implants and suggest them for people who cannot grow arms.[2][3]
claims.experts: No published studies have examined arm implants for this purpose.
